### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **139** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**97** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f`.

⛔ **20** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `requiredPermissions (symbol, 38 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 55 pages)`
- **28** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **186** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cc23f840bfff76f2653e32bdf1306ec77dacdb5b` — the merge of head `01d65d851b20fb39c1f6dd14946a91806da7ee42` into base `121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cc23f840bfff76f2653e32bdf1306ec77dacdb5b && git checkout cc23f840bfff76f2653e32bdf1306ec77dacdb5b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f 01d65d851b20fb39c1f6dd14946a91806da7ee42 && git checkout -B drift-repro 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f && git merge --no-ff 01d65d851b20fb39c1f6dd14946a91806da7ee42

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `17f7933a660b8e4b4bc74889876d54e070851b1c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-environment-user-outbox.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/environment-user-host.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/environment-user-outbox.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-users.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-ban-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-marker.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/manifest.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.ts, content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx (the environment-user host and outbox paragraphs)

Inputs read: card #33228 (body and its four comments), the ruling text on #33181 comment 6870710213, PR #34162 (body, 46 files, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on this head. The rest of the diff (tests, generated translation bundles, censuses, the cli inventory row, the changeset prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on this head when read: 28 concluded `success`, 10 `skipped`, 0 failed, 27 still running (Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Type Check · workspace, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI). Concluded green: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates and every other Lint family, Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Build Core, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI. ⛔ No test shard had concluded: this record judges the design and the concluded gates, and the test verdict is still owed by the shards.

### ① Derived judgments

- **New route `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/remove-sso-user`**: a widening. Right. It has its `AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER` row, both dogfood admin sweeps classify it, and it sits behind the same `gateAdmin` as the two add doors.
- **`EnvironmentUserHost.userRemoved?` and `EnvironmentUserEvent.deliveryId?`**: optional, additive. Right. A host built before this change keeps working through the `userDeactivated` fallback.
- **`EnvironmentUserEventKind` gains `'removed'`**: a widened exported union (`index.ts` re-exports `environment-user-host.ts`). Right as a widening; a host that switches exhaustively on the kind sees a compile error, which is the intended signal.
- **`invitation: { id, status }` on the add, import, ban, unban and remove answers**: additive. Right. No existing answer field changes.
- **New object `sys_environment_user_outbox`**: registered in `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` in sorted position, exported from `identity/index.ts`, registered by `authIdentityObjects`, listed in the deployment-level no-tenant test and the ADR-0131 inventory. Right.
- **Accept sets**: no existing door refuses anything it accepted. `ban-user` keeps its 503 on an unanswered host, `unban-user` stays fail-open. Right: no narrowing arm is owed.
- **Engine writes**: every compare-and-set write is spelled `{ where: { id, extra key }, multi: true }`, which `resolveEngineUpdateDispatch` routes to `driver.updateMany` (the #11009 compare-and-set spelling), and every write runs under `isSystem`, which the static read-only strip exempts. Right: the claim and the settlement are real conditional writes, and the all-`readonly` fields do not drop them.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on plugin-auth, platform-objects, spec and cli, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in both the PR body and the changeset. This matches the diff: nothing a metadata author can write changes, and AGENTS.md gives a non-protocol widening `patch`. The four packages are the four the diff moves. `Check Changeset` concluded `success`. Agreed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier H**: 3368 added lines, over 3000. Landing needs os-zhuang's approval after this record; `Check PR Size` and the queue guard stay whole-PR.
- **`open_questions`**: empty in the `os-dev-report` (comment 6902462660). Nothing to answer.
- **Flag: out-of-surface registrations** (`platform-object-names.ts`, the cli inventory, the two tenancy censuses): required by the conformance gates for a new platform object. Accepted.
- **Flag: no explicit admin audit row for a removal**: read in the tree. The delete runs under `authSystemWriteContext()` inside `runAttributedToUser`, so it carries the administrator as `attributedUserId`. Accepted as stated.
- **Flag: where the outbox lives** (the card left host-owned versus framework object to the maintainer): the claim comment reads the ruling's "Execution terms for the environment" as environment-side, and the diff builds that. The ruling text supports it ("mirror `sys_environment_revocation`"). Accepted; no escalation.
- **`security_findings: withheld`** in the report: nothing was handed to this review. See the first should-fix below, stated in rule terms.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts` (hits).** One name added to the `platform-objects` group, which the file's own maintenance contract requires for any object a platform package registers. Its first consumer is the cross-reference check that tells a real `sys_` name from a typo; the name matches the object's `name` and the constant in `environment-user-outbox.ts`. Holds.

**Ruled terms, against the tree.**

- "No database transaction is held across the invite call": holds. The add door writes the person and the `in_flight` row in one unit and calls the host after it. Ban, unban and remove call the host before their write. The re-add and the worker call it with no unit open.
- The per-row synchronous 403 at the developer cap: holds. The door still makes the first call, a refused add is taken back out and its row reads `failed` with the host's code, and an import settles each row on its own.
- Ruling 5's owner/admin 409: holds. `ban-user` is unchanged (refusal answered, 503 on an unanswered host, nothing written). A refused removal removes no one and records nothing.
- "Deleting or deactivating a pending row cancels its cloud invitation": holds on the main paths, and fails on the edge path in the first should-fix.
- The remove door's refusals: off a managed kernel 409 before the body is read; unknown id 404; unknown key 400; a non-pending row 409 before any host call; a non-admin stops at `gateAdmin`. Holds, except for the timing gap in the second should-fix.
- The fallback: `hostMember` picks `userDeactivated` only for `removed` and only when `userRemoved` is not a function; the event carries `source: 'idp_pending'`. Holds.
- What the outbox stores: `event_json` holds the person's id, email and name, the administrator's id, their cloud user id and `impersonatedBy`. `last_error` holds a fixed sentence, or the host's own refusal sentence. No driver text and no token reaches either. Holds.
- The boot: `bootEnvironmentUserOutbox` returns before touching the engine unless a host is wired and `isCloudManaged()` is true; `destroy()` stops the worker. Holds.
- The lease: a pending row is claimed by a conditional write and a token read-back; a lapsed `in_flight` row is taken by its old token; a settlement writes only under the token it holds. Two workers that read the same row give one holder. Holds. Delivery is at least once, as the header says: a door call slower than the two-minute lease is sent again under the same `deliveryId`.

**Should-fix 1 — an invitation can be sent for a person who is deactivated while pending.** The invariant "a deactivated pending person holds no live invitation" is not held by the worker. `stillOwed` judges an `added` row by the pending marker alone and never reads `banned`, and `supersedeOpenOutboxRows` stops only rows in `pending`, so an `added` row in `in_flight` survives a deactivation. Separately, the remove door queues a fresh invitation after a failed removal without asking whether the person is deactivated, and without asking whether the host was told to cancel at all (it also queues one when the host was never reached, and the answer then says the invitation "had already been cancelled", which is false). This is the ruled term "deleting or deactivating a pending row cancels its cloud invitation" failing on an edge path. Fix: `stillOwed` treats a banned person as not owed an `added` row, and the re-send after a failed removal fires only when the host took the cancellation and the person is not deactivated.

**Should-fix 2 — the remove door's "pending only" check is not held at the write.** `runRemoveSsoUser` reads `source`, calls the host, then `takeBackPerson` deletes `sys_user` by id alone. A person whose first sign-in clears the marker during the host call is deleted with their grants and membership, although the door's contract is "refused for any row that is not pending". Fix: make the delete conditional on the marker (or re-read it inside the unit of work) and answer the 409 when it no longer holds.

**Should-fix 3 — on a kernel with a host wired that is not cloud-managed, the ban and unban doors queue rows no worker drains.** `adminBanDeps` passes the host wherever the option is set, and `recordAsk` writes whenever a host answered. The worker boots only on a cloud-managed kernel. There a reactivation the host did not take is written `pending`, the answer says `invitation: { status: 'pending' }` and the log says "The call is retried", and nothing retries it. The boot's own comment ("elsewhere no door writes a row") is false for these two doors. Fix: record only on a cloud-managed kernel, matching the boot.

**Nits.**

- The accepted trigger skips `in_flight` rows, so a person who signs in during a send keeps a row that reads `sent`.
- A pending row's claim is conditional on `status` alone. A worker holding a stale read can claim a row another worker has just settled back to `pending`, which sends it before its backoff and undercounts `attempts`.
- "Every call to the host about a person is recorded" (docs, the object's jsdoc, the module header) overstates: a non-pending deactivation and a refused ban, unban or removal write no row. The changeset words it correctly.
- The `environmentUserHost` option jsdoc in `auth-plugin.ts` still lists only add, deactivate and reactivate.
- A queued `removed` call can reach the host after the same address was added again as a new person. The event names the removed `userId`; the docs should tell a host to cancel by `userId` or `deliveryId`, not by address.
- The boot runs inside the `kernel:ready` block whose `catch` swallows everything, so a worker that fails to start says nothing.

**Per file.** `sys-environment-user-outbox.object.ts`: agrees with the worker (statuses, kinds, numeric `next_attempt_at` and `claimed_until`, `user_id` as text so the row outlives the person, `get` / `list` only, `manage_platform_settings`). `environment-user-host.ts`: agrees. `environment-user-outbox.ts`: agrees except should-fix 1 and the nits. `pending-sso-users.ts`: agrees except should-fixes 1 and 2. `admin-ban-endpoints.ts`: agrees except should-fix 3. `pending-sso-marker.ts`, `manifest.ts`, `auth-route-ledger.ts`: agree. `auth-plugin.ts`: agrees, with the jsdoc and boot nits. `authentication.mdx`: agrees with the code sentence by sentence, apart from the "every call" nit.

No must-fix. The three should-fixes earn a delta review of their fix.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `01d65d851b20fb39c1f6dd14946a91806da7ee42`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-environment-user-outbox.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/environment-user-host.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/environment-user-outbox.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-users.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-ban-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-marker.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/manifest.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.ts, content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx (the environment-user host and outbox paragraphs)

Delta review of record 6902610047 for the hop 17f7933a..01d65d85: the fix commit 9bb42bbd, and the merge 01d65d85 of `main` at ea6de745. Read from the tree; the card thread's fix notes were not read.

Check-runs on this head when read: 13 concluded `success`, 11 `skipped`, 0 failed, 25 still running. Concluded green: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links. ⛔ Still running: every Lint family, every Type Check family, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI and Test Core 1/8 to 8/8. No lint, type or test verdict exists on this head yet; this record judges the design and the concluded gates, and those verdicts are still owed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept sets and public surface**: unchanged from the first record. The fix adds no route, no host member and no answer field.
- **`notifyEnvironmentUserHost` gains an optional fifth argument `opts.retried`**: an exported function, additive, and it only chooses a log sentence. Right.
- **`AdminBanEndpointDeps.isCloudManaged?`**: optional; absent reads as not managed, so nothing is recorded. Right: this is the safe default.
- **New refusal sentences** (`removeRefusedNotReinvited`, `removeHostCancelled`, `removeHostUnconfirmed`): message text on existing 409 and engine-refusal answers. No status or code changes. Right.
- **Net diff outside the fix**: unmoved. The PR still changes the same 46 files against `main`; for each of the 35 files the fix commit does not touch, the patch against the new base is identical to the patch against the old base.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `patch` on the same four packages, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset body was reworded to match the fix and now says which calls are recorded. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head. Agreed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier H**: still over 3000 lines (3663 added against `main`). Landing needs os-zhuang's approval after this record.
- **`open_questions`**: none were open, and the fix raises none.
- **The merge carries code from neither parent.** `git show --cc 01d65d85` shows one conflicted file, `pending-sso-users.ts`. The conflict itself (the `logger` type on `PendingSsoUserDeps`) is resolved correctly: it keeps this branch's `wakeOutbox` and takes `main`'s wider logger type, which is a superset of what this branch used. Beyond that, the merge commit adds eight lines that exist in neither parent: `userId` is passed into `removalNotDone`, and a removal that fails with a 5xx is now logged at `error` (or `warn`) with its cause. The lines are benign and match `main`'s new rule that a generic 500 answer logs its cause once, but they are new behaviour inside a merge commit. Flagged for the seat; not a defect in the tree.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts` (hits).** Not touched in this hop. Still holds.

**Should-fix 1 (an invitation for a deactivated pending person): closed.**

- `stillOwed` now answers `superseded` for an `added` or `reactivated` row whose person is deactivated, before it reads the pending marker.
- A deactivation and a removal now supersede `in_flight` rows as well as `pending` ones. A row whose sender is still mid-call can be written back by that sender's settlement, but it then returns as `pending` and meets the `stillOwed` check, so it is not sent.
- After a failed removal, a new invitation is queued only when the host took the cancellation and the person, re-read at that moment, is still pending and not deactivated. An unreadable person reads as deactivated, so nothing is sent.
- When the host was never reached, nothing is queued and the answer says the cancellation was not confirmed. The false "had already been cancelled" sentence is gone.
- Tried again: deactivate, then a refused removal; a sender that died mid-call followed by a deactivation; a deactivation landing between the re-read and the worker's send. Each ends with no invitation sent.

**Should-fix 2 (pending only, held at the write): closed.** The marker is re-read as the first step inside the removal's unit of work, and a person who is no longer pending is answered 409 and kept, with their grants and membership. The host call is no longer inside the gap. What remains is a check followed by a delete inside one unit, not a conditional delete; see the nits.

**Should-fix 3 (rows no worker drains off a managed kernel): closed.** `recordAsk` returns before any write unless `isCloudManaged()` is true, `adminBanDeps` passes the accessor, and the "The call is retried" log sentence is now printed only where a row is written. The boot comment matches the doors.

**Nits the author reports fixed.**

- Which calls are recorded: fixed in the docs, the object's jsdoc, the module header and the changeset. They now say invitations, re-sends and cancellations on a cloud-managed environment, and that a signed-in person's deactivation is asked but not recorded.
- The `environmentUserHost` option jsdoc in `auth-plugin.ts`: fixed. It names removal, the fallback and the outbox.
- Cancel by `userId` or `deliveryId`, never by address: fixed in the docs and the changeset.
- A worker that fails to start: fixed. The boot has its own `try`, and a failure is logged at `error` instead of falling into the silent `catch`.

**New in the fix, tried against the same invariants. Nits only.**

- A person who signs in while the host is asked is kept, and the cancellation the host took is then recorded as a `removed` / `sent` row. That row is newer than their `accepted` row, so "the newest row is the invitation status" reads "cancelled" for a person who is active. The host was also told to cancel an invitation that had just been accepted; what it does with that is the host's contract.
- The pending re-read and the delete are two statements in one unit of work. A sign-in that commits between them is still deleted. The gap is now a few statements, down from the length of a host call.
- A row removed by someone else between the first read and the re-read is answered 409 "not pending", where 404 would be exact.
- The remove door always passes `retried: true`, so its log says "The call is retried" even when the unit of work then fails and no row is kept. The answer to the administrator says the opposite, correctly.
- Still open from the first record: the accepted trigger skips `in_flight` rows, and a pending row's claim is conditional on `status` alone.

**Per file.** `environment-user-outbox.ts`, `pending-sso-users.ts`, `admin-ban-endpoints.ts`, `environment-user-host.ts`, `pending-sso-marker.ts`, `auth-plugin.ts`, `sys-environment-user-outbox.object.ts` and `authentication.mdx` now agree with the contract sentence by sentence, apart from the nits above. `manifest.ts` and `auth-route-ledger.ts` are unchanged in this hop and still agree.

No must-fix and no should-fix. Nits alone end the round.
